svg.text: PostgreSQL splits the problem, and neither half is a developer cluster tool
Packaging provisions one node and knows nothing about replicas; the multi-node capability lives in the test harness and never surfaces.
packaging — pg_createcluster
Debian postgresql-common, not upstream
pg_createcluster [options] VERSION NAME
version is positional — several majors side by side
--datadir · --port · --locale · --start-conf
operated afterwards by pg_ctlcluster / pg_lsclusters
no standby, no replica, no multi-node
single-cluster provisioning by construction
D5 observability: n/a — it is packaging
audience: an administrator on a Debian host
in-tree harness — PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster
src/test/perl/ — consumed by TAP tests
$primary.backup('bkp');
$standby.init_from_backup($primary, 'bkp');
$standby.enable_streaming($primary);
$standby.start;
the same three-step chain CUBRID assembles by hand
(backupdb → copy → restoreslave) — inherent to
physical replication, only the interface is missing
fault verbs present: kill9 · promote · stop('immediate')
binaries: install_path — local build is first-class
no network disruption method — connstr / raw_connect only
and no user-facing surface: it is a Perl API, not a CLI
Implication for CUBRID (01-01 §4 I1): a harness can own the primitives, but the developer-facing surface still has to be built on top —
which is why cubrid-testkit consuming cluster-sandbox, rather than owning provisioning, is the cleaner split.
